jurisdictions.reason: Five familiar names. Avalon Peninsula and Labrador use whole census divisions; Central, Western and Eastern currently contain 18 explicitly evidenced communities. Remaining municipalities stay directly under the province until a full crosswalk is qualified. Selected-community outlines are footprints, not full regions.
Three geographic counties; these browsing areas do not imply county governments.
Eighteen geographic counties. Halifax, Queens and Cape Breton county geography remains distinct from the similarly named regional municipalities.
Twelve regional service commission geographies from the post-reform 2025 source.
Seventeen régions administratives; a draft crosswalk groups the existing municipal outlines. MRCs are retained as source divisions, not substituted for administrative regions.

Forty named county, regional municipality and territorial district geographies. Nine generic census divisions are left without a region, including single-tier city equivalents. Separated cities and reserves in geographic counties do not become county-government members.

Eight familiar geographic groupings supported by the Manitoba Arts Council map and census-division crosswalk. Winnipeg groups Winnipeg and Headingley (2025 division 11), not the full metropolitan region. Boundaries are derived from 2025 CSDs.

Intentional province-to-municipality browsing. Recognized local descriptions such as Southwest Saskatchewan exist, but a coherent default regional scheme and reproducible membership evidence have not been qualified. Marketing travel zones and numbered census divisions are not substitutes. All 995 CSDs remain directly accessible.

evidence.claim: Four travel zones are explicitly created for tourism marketing; they are not adopted as familiar geographic regions.
Southwest Saskatchewan is used locally. Deferral does not mean that Saskatchewan has no recognized local regions.

jurisdictions.reason: Peace Country (Alberta portion) and Central Alberta are represented by 27 selected municipal CSDs supported by resident-facing municipal references and regional organizations. The remaining 392 CSDs are directly accessible under Alberta. Neither watersheds nor the full membership territory of a business alliance is treated as the cultural-region boundary.

Twenty-seven regional district geographies plus Stikine, explicitly typed as an unincorporated region. Northern Rockies remains at municipal level; its census division is not added as a duplicate regional district. These are geographic groupings, including separately governed Indigenous areas.

Klondike, Kluane and Southern Lakes contain 11 explicitly listed community CSDs. The remaining 22 CSDs stay directly under Yukon. Neither the territory-wide unorganized CSD nor Indigenous territories are assigned by inference. Outlines are community footprints; the nine wilderness-statistics regions are not substituted for the different visitor regions.

Five MACA regional community groupings, covering 33 listed CSDs. Eight unlisted or unorganized CSDs remain directly under the territory. Outlines are selected community footprints, not complete administrative or Indigenous territorial boundaries.
Qikiqtaaluk, Kivalliq and Kitikmeot geographic regions. This does not model Inuit land ownership or governance.

evidence.claim: 2026-2027 list supports the selected towns and core municipal districts. Alliance membership is evidence of regional association, not a definition of the entire Peace Country.
Resident-facing description places Grande Prairie in the Peace Region.

regions.name: Central Alberta
regions.relationship_basis: Geographic browsing membership from the cited public reference; no administrative jurisdiction is asserted.
regions.coverage_note: Selected communities and counties supported by municipal and regional references. Outlines show their combined municipal footprints, not the complete Central Alberta boundary. Nearby communities and separate Indigenous CSDs are not assigned merely because they are surrounded by a county.

evidence.claim: Published municipal representation supports selected Central Alberta communities and counties; it does not establish an exhaustive cultural-region boundary.
Municipal description identifies Red Deer with Central Alberta.
Municipal description places Blackfalds in Central Alberta.
Municipal planning document describes Sylvan Lake as located in Central Alberta.
Resident-facing municipal amenities page places the city’s sports facilities in Central Alberta.
